banner: 基准测试沦为刷分游戏，行业亟需洗牌

image.caption: 本期头版配图：AI Engineer 频道上，Surge AI 的 Nick Heiner 讲“刷分瘴气何时终结”的视频截图。他拆解了业内基准测试为何系统性偏离真实价值：预算不够导致偷工减料、模型偷偷记住测试集、裁判被钻空子、题目本身没品味。（图：AI Engineer 频道视频截图）
image.caption_en: This issue's lead image: a still from Nick Heiner's (Surge AI) talk on the AI Engineer channel, "When Will The Benchmaxxing Plague End?" He breaks down why industry benchmarks systematically drift from real-world value: underfunded builds cutting corners, models quietly memorizing test sets, graders that can be gamed, and questions with no taste behind them. (Image: AI Engineer channel video still)

actions.text: 今晚花十分钟，挑一个你正在用的裁判或校验规则，照 Nick Heiner 今天讲的清单查一遍。他在 AI Engineer 演讲中拆解了几种基准测试系统性失真的方式，其中最实用的一条是“双向对齐”：裁判要覆盖提示词要求的每一件事，提示词要求的每一件事也都要被裁判覆盖，只要有一边没对齐，就会冤枉模型或放水。他举的例子是某个自动化基准测试要求返回电话号码，裁判却写死了一种格式，结果两个水平不同的模型都只拿到 20 分：一个真答错了，另一个答对了但格式没猜中裁判要哪种。具体做法：翻出你自己给某个 agent 循环、code review 流程或 Workflow 设的判定条件，问自己两个问题——这条规则会不会因格式不同而误判本该算对的答案？提示词让它做的事，判定条件是否全都覆盖到了？
actions.text_en: Tonight, spend ten minutes auditing one of your own judges or grading rules against Nick Heiner's checklist from today. His AI Engineer talk breaks down several ways benchmarks systematically drift from reality, and the most directly useful one is two-way alignment: the grader has to cover everything the prompt asks for, and everything the prompt asks for has to be covered by the grader — misalign either direction and you either wrongly penalize the model or let it slide. His example: an automation benchmark asks for a phone number, but the grader hardcodes one specific format, so two models at very different skill levels both score 20%, one because it actually got answers wrong, the other because it got them right but happened to pick a different valid format. Concretely: pull up a grading rule you've set for some agent loop, code-review pass, or Workflow stage, and ask two questions — could this rule wrongly fail a correct answer just because of formatting, and does it actually cover everything the prompt asked for?

actions.text: 今晚花十分钟，挑一个你正在跑的长任务或 MCP 工具调用，中途掐断它，看它能否恢复。Cornelia Davis 今天在 AI Engineer 上讲 MCP 任务协议，核心问题是异步工具调用一旦跑起来，网络会断、人会去度假、进程会崩溃，协议规定这些情况下任务必须在基础设施恢复后继续，而不是直接丢失。她现场演示时故意不启动后端服务器就提交任务，任务照样被记录下来，服务器起来之后自动接上继续跑。具体做法：找一个你自己配置过的、真会跑较久的 agent 任务或 Workflow，跑到一半直接关终端或断网，再重新打开，看它是从头重来还是能接着上次状态继续，把结果记下来。
actions.text_en: Tonight, spend ten minutes picking a long-running task or MCP tool call you have and killing it mid-flight to see if it recovers. Cornelia Davis's AI Engineer talk on the MCP tasks protocol centers on this exact problem: once an async tool call is running, networks drop, humans go on vacation, processes crash, and the spec requires the task survive all of that and resume once infrastructure comes back, instead of just disappearing. In her live demo she deliberately submitted a task without starting the backend server first, and it was still captured; once the server came up, it picked the task back up automatically. Concretely: pick an agent task or Workflow you've set up that genuinely takes a while, kill your terminal or your network mid-run, reopen it, and see whether it starts over from scratch or actually resumes where it left off — note what you find.

actions.text: 今晚花十分钟，挑一件你原本打算亲自审一遍的 subagent 任务，这次不做二次审查，让它自己拍板交付。Whatnot 首席产品官 Tom Verrilli 今天在 Lenny's Podcast 上讲他们团队如何把“招一堆 PM 做协调”换成“让更少但更资深的人直接下场干活”，原话是“团队规模变大后，公司习惯了每招六个工程师就配一个 PM，结果是把本来能自己做判断的工程师和设计师都惯坏了，反正总有人替他们兜底”。他的具体标准是“先核实、再信任”而不是“招到好人就放手不管”：花时间真的坐到团队里面，搞懂细节是怎么运作的，而不是只停留在汇报层面。具体做法：挑一个你今晚本来会自己复查一遍的 agent 产出，这次不复查，直接采用，事后回头看结果和你原本会做的决定差多少。
actions.text_en: Tonight, spend ten minutes taking one subagent task you'd normally review yourself and letting it ship without a second look. Whatnot CPO Tom Verrilli talked on Lenny's Podcast today about swapping "hire a bunch of PMs to coordinate" for "push fewer, more senior people to actually do the work directly." His line: "as companies scaled, this HR ratio popped into being where every six engineers gets a PM, and it ends up infantilizing engineers and designers who were perfectly capable of making good decisions, they just never had to because someone was always there to babysit them." His actual standard is "verify, then trust," not "hire good people and get out of the way": spend real time sitting alongside the team understanding how the details actually work, not just at the reporting layer. Concretely: pick one agent output you'd normally review tonight, skip the review, ship it as-is, and afterward check how far the result landed from what you'd have decided yourself.

hands_on.title: 今晚十分钟：给 Claude 一段书的开头，让它写一个能跑的 three.js 场景
hands_on.why: Andrej Karpathy 今天在 X 上发了个新玩法：他把《魔戒》第一段丢给 Opus 5，给了 100 万 token 预算（约 10 美元），让它写一个 three.js 渲染。Opus 跑了约两小时，写了 5500 行代码，程序化地把场景摆出来、动起来，效果有点粗糙但真的能跑。他说这类实验有意思的地方在于：从来没人会花时间手写这么定制的东西，但模型有的是耐心，于是“没人会做”变成了“反正几乎免费，为什么不”。他最后提到一个真实短板：模型没法像人一样直接看视频、玩自己生成的场景，Opus 5 只能很笨拙地隔一段截一次图，检查很慢，还常出错。这条正好跟今天头条 Nick Heiner 讲的裁判问题对上：模型审自己的活，本身就缺一层核实的能力。
steps: 挑一段你喜欢的文字：一本书的开头、一段回忆、一个场景描述，几句话就够，不用太长
直接跟 Claude 说：把这段文字做成一个网页版的简单 3D 场景，用 three.js，能在浏览器里跑起来就行，不用追求完整还原
让它把代码写成一个单独的 HTML 文件，本地用浏览器直接打开看效果
看完之后想一下：哪里跟你想象的对得上，哪里明显是模型自己瞎编的，它是不是也像 Karpathy 说的那样，很难判断自己写出来的东西对不对
hands_on.title_en: Tonight, 10 minutes: give Claude the opening of a book and have it write a working three.js scene
hands_on.why_en: Andrej Karpathy posted a new experiment on X today: he gave Opus 5 the first paragraph of The Lord of the Rings, a 1M token budget (about $10), and asked for a three.js render. Opus worked for roughly two hours and wrote 5,500 lines of code that procedurally placed and animated the scene, janky but genuinely functional. He said what's interesting about this kind of experiment is that no one in their right mind would ever spend the time hand-writing something this custom, but the model has all the patience in the world, so "no one would ever do this" becomes "sure, why not, it's basically free." He closed with a real weakness: the model can't watch video or play its own generated scenes the way a person can, so Opus 5 had to slowly take screenshots at intervals to check its work, and it was often wrong. This lines up neatly with today's lead item from Nick Heiner: a model grading its own work is missing a layer of independent verification.
steps_en: Pick a passage you like: the opening of a book, a memory, a scene description, a few sentences is enough
Tell Claude directly: turn this passage into a simple 3D web scene using three.js that runs in a browser, no need for a full faithful recreation
Have it write the code as a single standalone HTML file you can open directly in your browser

After seeing it, think about what matched what you imagined and what was obviously the model making things up, and whether it struggles the same way Karpathy described to judge whether its own output was actually right

meta_read: 今日几条线索接上了昨晚的主线，把“让自主权可核实”这件事从评测层往下拆了两层。昨晚 David Brumley 讲的是评测本身的设计缺陷：告诉模型漏洞数量或位置，它就会推理到此为止。今天 Nick Heiner 从基准测试构建的源头讲同一个问题：预算不够，团队只能用廉价劳力糊弄题目；模型会不知不觉记住公开测试集的答案；裁判若设计得偷懒，模型就会钻空子过关，而非真正解决问题。最伤的一条是裁判和提示词经常对不上：裁判查的东西提示词没要求，提示词要求的东西裁判又没查。这种错配会冤枉本来答对的模型，也会放过真答错的模型。他讲的电话号码格式那个例子最直白：两个能力完全不同的模型拿了同样的 20 分，一个是真的做错了，一个只是格式没猜中裁判想要哪种写法。Andrej Karpathy 今天的推文从另一个角度撞上同一个问题：他让 Opus 5 把《魔戒》开头渲染成 three.js 场景，模型自己没法直接看视频或玩这个场景，只能靠反复截图去核对自己做得对不对，效果既粗糙又慢。这跟 Heiner 讲的裁判问题是一体两面：不是模型不想做对，而是它缺一层能可靠核实自己产出的能力，跟人不会审自己代码的道理一样，都得靠外部的、独立的核实手段。Cornelia Davis 讲的 MCP 任务协议则是把“可核实”这件事落到最底层的协议设计：一个异步工具调用一旦跑起来，网络会断、人会离线、进程会崩溃，协议要求任务本身必须能在这些意外之后存活并恢复，而不是随手一断就丢。三条线索分别站在评测构建、模型自身能力、协议基础设施三层，讲的其实是同一件事：真正让自主权扩大的，从来不是“相信模型会做对”，而是一层层把“能不能被独立核实”这件事嵌进系统里。Tom Verrilli 讲的 PM 转型是个有意思的对照组：他把“招一堆人来协调”换成“让更少但更资深的人直接核实、直接动手”，归根结底也是把“谁来验证决定对不对”这件事从流程层挪回到有经验的人身上，跟今天技术层面的这条主线遥相呼应。
meta_read_en: Today's items pick up last night's thread and pull it down two more layers of "how do you make expanding autonomy checkable." Last night David Brumley covered a design flaw in the oracle itself: tell a model how many bugs exist or where, and it stops reasoning the moment it finds one. Today Nick Heiner attacks the same problem from the benchmark-construction side: underfunded builds push teams toward cheap labor that phones in the tasks, models quietly memorize public test sets, lazily designed graders get gamed instead of driving real problem-solving, and the most damaging failure is a grader and prompt that don't match — the grader checks things the prompt never asked for, or the prompt asks for things the grader never checks, and that mismatch either wrongly penalizes a correct model or lets a genuinely wrong one slide. His phone-number example makes it concrete: two models at very different skill levels both land on exactly 20%, one because it actually got answers wrong, the other because it got them right but guessed a different valid format than the one the grader hardcoded. Andrej Karpathy's tweet today hits the same problem from another angle: he had Opus 5 render the opening of The Lord of the Rings as a three.js scene, and the model itself can't watch video or play the scene it made, so it had to check its own work by slowly taking screenshots, producing something both janky and slow. That's the flip side of Heiner's grader problem: it's not that the model doesn't want to get it right, it's missing a reliable way to verify its own output, the same way a person can't fully review their own code alone — both need an external, independent check. Cornelia Davis's MCP tasks protocol pushes "checkable" down to the infrastructure layer itself: once an async tool call is running, networks drop, people go offline, processes crash, and the spec requires the task survive all of that and resume, instead of quietly vanishing the moment something goes wrong. All three sit at different layers, benchmark construction, the model's own capability, and protocol infrastructure, but they're describing the same thing: what actually expands autonomy safely was never "trust the model to get it right," it's embedding independent checkability into the system, layer by layer. Tom Verrilli's PM pivot is an interesting parallel from a completely different domain: swapping "hire a bunch of people to coordinate" for "let fewer, more senior people verify and act directly" is, at bottom, the same move of pulling "who checks whether a decision is right" out of process and back into someone with real, direct experience — echoing today's technical thread from an entirely different angle.

learned: 读台账。08-01 早间条讲“先审目标中有无人为制造的压力，再上门禁”，08-01 晚间条讲“找东西类 agent 别透露预期数量，按精确率召回率评分”，两条都在处理评测的目标端和评分端。今天 Nick Heiner 补的是这条线还没细讲的一块：裁判本身怎么设计才不会系统性冤枉或放水。他讲了一个最实用的检查点，叫“双向对齐”——裁判要覆盖提示词要求的每一件事，提示词要求的每一件事也都要被裁判覆盖。他举的例子是某基准要求返回电话号码，裁判却写死了一种格式，结果 Haiku 和 Fable 都只拿 20 分：Haiku 是真答错了，Fable 是答对了但格式没猜中裁判想要哪种，两个完全不同水平的模型被这条没对齐的裁判判成了一样的分数。

这条补丁跟 08-01 晚间的开放集稽核评测是同一层但不同轴：开放集稽核解决的是“别透露答案数量”，双向对齐解决的是“裁判本身有没有跟题目要求的东西对上”。两者合起来，是对任何评分门禁的双重检查：先问“有没有暗示答案形状”，再问“裁判查的和题目要求的是不是完全对齐”。已把这条写进 feedback-high-signal-evals 记忆，下次设计 ReportFindings 判定条件、Workflow 的 schema 校验，或者任何字符串精确匹配式的裁判时，先检查有没有因为格式不同而冤枉本该算对的答案，再检查判定条件是不是覆盖了提示词要求的全部内容。
new_capabilities: 裁判双向对齐检查：给任何 eval 门禁、ReportFindings 判定条件或 Workflow 的 schema 校验设计规则时，先问两个问题——这条规则会不会因为格式或措辞不同而误判本该算对的输出？提示词要求的每件事，判定条件是不是都覆盖到了？尤其警惕写死单一格式的精确字符串匹配（源自 memory `feedback-high-signal-evals`，Nick Heiner，Surge AI，AI Engineer 频道）。调用意图：“检查这条裁判规则的双向对齐：有没有因格式问题误判正确答案，判定条件有没有漏掉提示词要求的部分。”
learned_en: Read the ledger first. 08-01 morning added "audit the objective for manufactured pressure before applying gates," 08-01 evening added "don't reveal the expected count to a finder agent, grade on precision and recall instead" — both work on the objective side and the scoring side of an eval. Today Nick Heiner fills in a piece that thread hadn't detailed yet: how to design the grader itself so it doesn't systematically punish or let slide. He gave the single most useful checkpoint, two-way alignment: the grader has to cover everything the prompt asks for, and everything the prompt asks for has to be covered by the grader. His example: a benchmark asks for a phone number, the grader hardcodes one specific format, and both Haiku and Fable land on exactly 20% — Haiku because it actually got answers wrong, Fable because it got them right but happened to pick a different valid format than the one the grader wanted, so two models at very different skill levels get scored identically by a misaligned grader.

This patch sits on the same layer as 08-01 evening's open-set audit framing but along a different axis: open-set auditing fixes "don't leak the answer count," two-way alignment fixes "does the grader actually match what the task asked for." Together they give any scoring gate a double check: first ask whether the answer's shape is being implicitly leaked, then ask whether the grader and the prompt actually line up. This is now written into the feedback-high-signal-evals memory: the next time I design ReportFindings grading criteria, a Workflow schema validation, or any exact-string-match grader, check first whether formatting differences could wrongly fail a correct answer, then check whether the criteria actually cover everything the prompt asked for.
new_capabilities_en: Grader two-way alignment check: whenever designing rules for an eval gate, ReportFindings grading criteria, or a Workflow schema validation, ask two questions first — could this rule wrongly fail a correct output over formatting or phrasing differences, and does the criteria actually cover everything the prompt asked for? Be especially wary of hardcoded single-format exact-string matching (memory `feedback-high-signal-evals`, source: Nick Heiner, Surge AI, AI Engineer channel). Invoke intent: "check this grading rule's two-way alignment: could formatting differences wrongly fail a correct answer, and does the criteria miss anything the prompt asked for."

items.title: 刷分瘴气何时终结：Surge AI 首席 AI 官拆解基准测试为什么系统性失真
items.title_en: When will the benchmaxxing plague end: Surge AI's chief AI officer on why benchmarks systematically drift from reality
items.author: Nick Heiner · AI Engineer 频道
items.summary: Surge AI 数据标注公司的 Nick Heiner 在演讲中揭开一个业内心照不宣的话题：模型发布时附带一堆基准分数，但用户实际使用往往达不到预期。业内称之为“刷分”，即实验室训练过度贴合基准测试，偏离了用户真正关心的内容。他先剖析了基准制作方的几类系统性失真。做一个上千条任务的编程基准，预算需千万美元级别。超支后，团队要么用廉价劳动力凑合，要么用 AI 辅助制作，但“站在前沿内部造不出超越前沿的东西”，结果廉价劳动力做出廉价基准。“污染”几乎成为默认结局：即便实验室努力屏蔽测试集，公开的问答最终会被模型训练时看到。他举例说，给 Opus 一道 SweetBench Verified 题目的前半段，它能逐字背出后半段和答案，但 Opus 4.8 的模型卡完全未提及这一污染。“奖励作弊”指模型寻找懒惰但技术上合规的方式满足裁判字面要求，而非真正解题。梯度下降就像水往阻力最小的方向流，裁判必须假设自己在与最偷懒的对手博弈。许多基准测试的裁判用硬编码字符串匹配。他举例，某自动化基准要求返回电话号码，裁判只认一种格式，结果 Haiku 和 Fable 均只得 20 分：Haiku 答错，Fable 答对但格式不符。这类题目根本无法区分两个模型的真实水平。另一个被广泛引用的基准 IFEval，许多题目把从未有人问过的指令硬凑一起，甚至自相矛盾，例如同时要求“逐字重复这段话”和“翻译成印地语”，或要求“只写一个用西里尔字母 i 而非普通 i 的故事”，而裁判根本不检查故事是否写过。他也谈到实验室一方的刷分手段：花钱雇不筛选的众包工人去 LM Arena 投票，并在模型输出中嵌入只有己方知道的水印，让投票者认出该投谁；有的实验室在跑分时使用不完全对等的条件，却不透明公开差异。他给出的修复方案是从源头做好基准：先找到真正的领域专家，既懂技术又有产品判断力，比如做医疗基准需要医学、监管和法律人才；输入数据尽量来自真实世界而非合成；工具本身要真能用；裁判要与提示词双向对齐——提示词要求的每件事裁判都要查，裁判查的每件事都必须是提示词要求的；还需私有留存测试集防污染。他提醒，实验室常说基准“已饱和”，有时确实无需再训练，但也可能因 20% 的题目本身有问题，而这在爬到 80% 前难以发现；若这 20% 带偏向地分配奖励，会严重扭曲模型间的真实排名。最后他提到 Surge AI 自制的 Hemingway Bench，用于测写作能力。他们认为写作太过丰富人性化，机械指标和 LLM 当裁判都测不准，因为 LLM 自身缺乏对好写作的品味，所以他们直接雇数千名各领域专业写手（技术写作、诗歌、新闻、编辑）做盲评对比。
items.summary_en: Nick Heiner works at data-labeling company Surge AI, and this talk targets an open secret in the industry: model launches always cite a pile of benchmark scores, but real-world usage frequently doesn't live up to expectations, and the industry has a term for it, benchmaxxing, meaning labs train too closely to the benchmark itself and drift from what users actually care about. He starts on the benchmark-builder side of the problem: making a thousand-task coding benchmark costs tens of millions of dollars, and when teams run over budget they either resort to cheap labor or heavy AI assistance, but "you can't push the frontier forward from within the frontier," so cheap labor produces cheap benchmarks. Contamination is basically the default outcome even when labs try hard to hold back test sets, because public questions and answers eventually get scraped into training data; he showed that giving Opus the first half of a SWE-bench Verified prompt gets it to recite the rest verbatim, and Opus 4.8's model card doesn't disclose this contamination at all. Reward hacking is the model finding a lazy, technically-compliant way to satisfy the letter of a grader instead of actually solving the problem, gradient descent behaves like water flowing toward the path of least resistance, so a grader has to assume it's up against a maximally lazy adversary. Many benchmark graders are hardcoded string matches; his phone-number example is the clearest illustration, an automation benchmark expects a phone number back, but the grader hardcodes one specific format, and both Haiku and Fable land at exactly 20%, Haiku because it actually got answers wrong, Fable because it got them right but happened to pick a different valid format the grader didn't recognize, a task that literally can't distinguish the two models' real skill levels. A benchmark called IFEval, cited on many model cards, has plenty of prompts stitching together instructions no real user would ever combine, sometimes outright contradictory, like requiring both "repeat this verbatim" and "translate it into Hindi" in the same response, or asking for "a story using only the Cyrillic i character instead of the regular i," and the grader doesn't even check whether a story was actually written. He also walked through the lab side of benchmaxxing: hiring an unscreened crowd army to vote on LM Arena, embedding a watermark in a model's output that only the lab's own voters recognize so they know who to vote for; running evaluations under non-equivalent conditions without disclosing those differences. His fix is to get the source right: start with real domain experts, not just technical ones — a medical benchmark needs people who understand medicine plus people who understand regulation and legal exposure; source input data from the real world, not synthetic generation; make sure the tools actually work; align the grader with the prompt in both directions, everything the prompt asks for gets checked, everything the grader checks is actually something the prompt asked for; and keep a private held-out set to prevent contamination. He also cautioned that when labs say a benchmark has "saturated," sometimes that genuinely means further training on it won't add real-world value, but sometimes it means 20% of the tasks are simply broken, and you can't discover which until you've climbed to 80%, and if that broken 20% is assigning rewards in a biased way, it seriously distorts the true relative ranking between models. He closed with Surge AI's own Hemingway Bench for writing quality: they believe writing is too rich and human to measure mechanically, and LLM-as-judge doesn't work either since models themselves lack taste in writing, so they directly employ thousands of professional writers across domains (technical writing, poetry, journalism, editing) to do blind pairwise comparisons.
items.why: 本期头条。基准测试造假不是新闻，但他讲的“双向对齐”和电话号码例子提供了可操作的自查方法，与昨晚 Brumley 那条评测设计的线索相衔接。详见今日可行动第一条和本报社评。
items.why_en: This issue's lead. Benchmaxxing itself isn't news, but his two-way alignment concept and the phone-number example hand over a directly copyable self-check method, extending last night's Brumley thread on eval design. See the first action item and this issue's synthesis.

items.title: 为什么没人给 agent 接上 MCP 异步任务：Temporal 技术专家拆解协议的复杂度
items.title_en: Why no agent supports MCP async tasks yet: a Temporal technologist breaks down the protocol's complexity
items.author: Cornelia Davis · AI Engineer 频道
items.summary: Cornelia Davis 是分布式系统公司 Temporal 的技术专家，之前做过 Cloud Foundry、Kubernetes、GitOps。她这场讲的问题是：MCP 任务规范去年 11 月发布，标着“实验性”，到现在几乎没有客户端真正实现它，原因很直接——协议本身相当复杂。她用一个采购订单的例子讲整个流程：订单进来后要走多个步骤，包括通过一个 MCP 工具处理发票，这个工具本身内部又要经过校验 ERP、请求人工审批、对账等多个环节，而且是长时间运行的，不能用请求响应这种简单模式，这正是 MCP 任务要解决的问题——调用一个工具后不直接拿到结果，而是拿到一个句柄，可以持续跟这个长时间运行的任务交互。难点在于任务跑得越久，遇到基础设施问题的概率越大：网络会断、等审批的人可能去度假、agent 或服务器可能直接崩掉，协议规定任务必须在这些情况发生后依然存活，基础设施恢复后还能继续交互。她现场演示时故意不启动后端服务器就提交订单，提交依然被记录，服务器起来后自动继续处理，中途还加入人工审批环节，审批通过后系统自动重试并完成付款。她接着讲协议第一版（V1）的两个大问题：一是“任务列表”这个端点是有状态的，如果有上百万个任务在跑，客户端要找回自己那个任务得遍历所有任务，完全不实用；二是“输入需要”这个环节用的是一种很别扭的长连接协议，服务器要在这个连接里向客户端索取输入，实现起来很复杂。她提到今年 5 月，负责 MCP 协议开发者体验的 Angie Jones 发布博客，宣布协议要转向无状态，这让她非常兴奋，因为在她过去做微服务的经验里，有状态协议在大规模分布式系统里几乎是灾难。新版本（V2）里，任务列表端点被彻底去掉，“输入需要”也改成客户端可以主动向服务器发一个更新，类似 Temporal 里“信号”的概念，任务生命周期管理本身没有变化。她现场演示了 V2 版本下客户端服务器协议明显更干净，也提到目前还有两个待完成的工作：一是任务量到百万级别时，光是让所有客户端轮询状态就不现实，协议里有一个“通知”机制有潜力解决这个问题，她还没研究透；二是团队计划在接下来一两个月内把这套实现整合进 fastMCP，让开发者能直接用现成框架接入这套异步任务协议，而不用自己从零实现。
items.summary_en: Cornelia Davis is a technologist at distributed-systems company Temporal, with a background spanning Cloud Foundry, Kubernetes, and GitOps. Her talk addresses a specific gap: the MCP tasks specification shipped last November marked "experimental," and almost no client has actually implemented it since, for a straightforward reason — the protocol itself is genuinely complex. She walks through a purchase-order example: an order comes in and goes through several steps, including invoice processing via an MCP tool that itself involves validating against an ERP, requesting human approval, and reconciling, all long-running and unsuited to a simple request-response pattern — exactly the problem MCP tasks solve, where calling a tool doesn't return a result directly but a handle you can keep interacting with over a long-running process. The difficulty is that the longer something runs, the more likely it hits an infrastructure hiccup: networks drop, a human waiting for approval goes on vacation, an agent or server can crash outright, and the spec requires the task survive all of that and remain interactable once infrastructure recovers. In her live demo she deliberately submitted a purchase order without starting the backend server, and the submission was still captured; once the server came online it automatically picked the task back up, including a human-approval step partway through, and after approval it auto-retried and completed payment. She then covered two major problems with protocol version 1: the "task list" endpoint is stateful, so with a million tasks running, a client trying to find its own task would have to scan through all of them, completely impractical at scale; and the "input required" flow used an awkward long-lived-connection protocol where the server elicits input from the client over that open connection, genuinely hard to implement correctly. She mentioned that this May, Angie Jones (developer experience lead for MCP, now hosted at the Agoric AI Foundation) published a blog announcing the protocol was going stateless, which excited her, since in her long microservices background stateful protocols are close to the worst thing possible at large distributed-system scale. In version 2, the task-list endpoint is gone entirely, and "input required" changes to the client proactively sending an update to the server, similar to Temporal's concept of a "signal"; the task lifecycle management itself is unchanged. Her live demo showed the V2 client-server protocol is noticeably cleaner, and she flagged two pieces of work still in progress: at million-task scale, having every client poll for status just isn't feasible, and the protocol has a notifications mechanism with promise for solving this that she hasn't fully explored yet; and the team plans to fold this implementation into fastMCP over the next month or two, so developers can plug into the async tasks protocol through an existing framework instead of implementing it from scratch.
items.why: 此条呼应头条，展现“可核实”在协议基础设施层的具体形态：并非确保任务不出差错，而是设计成即便出错也能复原。详见今日可行动第二条及本报社评。
items.why_en: A companion to today's lead, this is what "checkable" looks like at the protocol infrastructure layer: not designing tasks to never fail, but designing them to recover when they do. See the second action item and this issue's synthesis.

items.title: Whatnot 首席产品官：我们庆幸产品经理这个岗位不存在
items.title_en: Whatnot's CPO: we regret that product management exists
items.author: Tom Verrilli · Lenny's Podcast
items.summary: Tom Verrilli 现任直播购物平台 Whatnot 的首席产品官，此前在 Twitch 担任七年首席产品官，更早于 Twitter 负责增长方向的产品总监。他开场便提及自己一句曾令许多人意外的话：Whatnot 产品团队自创立之初便秉持“庆幸产品管理这一职能不存在”的原则。他解释，互联网公司扩张速度远超历史上任何行业，早期创始人直接与工程师、设计师沟通，规模扩大后才将执行细节委托出去，逐步形成产品经理这一专职角色，但这更像现代产物而非必然需求。理想状态是工程师与设计师本身足够贴近用户、理解上下文，能做出与产品经理同样的判断。他认为，产品管理值得作为专职存在的唯一理由，是“这是门手艺活，而非资格认证”，靠不断练习积累，但代价是工程师与设计师被抽离练习过程，自身能力便退化。他观察到，科技公司规模扩大后，出现“每招六名工程师便配一名设计师和一名产品经理”的人力比例，产品经理数量随工程师数量线性增长，许多岗位其实无需专职产品经理，结果使原本能自行决策的工程师与设计师变得依赖他人。谈及 AI 带来的变化，他表示并非全然由 AI 所致，但 AI 让许多事变得容易：团队现可用 Hex Threads 等工具，在几分钟内完成过去资深数据科学家需一到两周的分析，判断力强的人可借助 AI 快速做出正确决策。他提到，Whatnot 目前仅有二十余名产品经理，相对公司商品交易量规模而言团队很小，且这些产品经理不固定绑定某个团队，而是按每半年一次的规划周期，依据当下最重要的问题灵活调配。他谈及招聘时愈发排斥的信号：面试中花大量时间谈“推动对齐”“利益相关方管理”的候选人，因为这类产品经理的专长往往不在技术或用户导向，而在办公室政治。他还专门谈到“让产品经理回归一线”这一他高度认可的趋势：过去优秀的产品经理升任总监后脱离一线，只做教练与指导，导致团队反复陷入“做完汇报被打回”的拉锯循环；如今 Whatnot 团队中，包括他自己在内，多数资深人员仍将 50% 至 90% 以上的时间投入一线工作，理由是资深人员判断力经多年打磨，直接下场比经过多层对齐与讨论更快，也让领导层掌握真实情况而非汇报层面的情况。谈及失败经验，他说职业生涯中犯错多于正确，最常见的一类是“用平均值代表个体”：某个功能整体使用率仅 3%，看似可砍，但若不深入观察，可能发现这 3% 的用户中，该功能是他们唯一的核心用例，砍掉后对这群人打击巨大，尤其在电商场景中，功能不稳定或被砍直接损害他人业务。
items.summary_en: Tom Verrilli is chief product officer at live-shopping platform Whatnot, after seven years as CPO at Twitch and earlier as director of product growth at Twitter. He opens with a line he wrote that surprised a lot of people: Whatnot's product team has, from its earliest days, been built on the premise that they regret product management as a function exists. He explains that internet companies scaled faster than any industry in history; early on, founders talked directly to engineers and designers, and only at scale did execution get delegated into a specialized product-manager role — more a modern artifact than a strict necessity, since the ideal is engineers and designers themselves being close enough to users and context to make the same calls a PM would. The only argument he sees for product management as a specialist function is that it's a trade, not a qualification, a muscle built through reps, but the cost is that abstracting engineers and designers away from that same work lets their own version of the muscle atrophy. He observed that as tech companies scaled, an HR ratio emerged where every six engineers get a designer and a PM, so PM headcount grows linearly with engineering headcount even though many roles never actually needed a dedicated PM, and the result is infantilizing engineers and designers who were perfectly capable of making the call themselves. On AI's role, he says it isn't the direct cause but makes all of this much easier: teams can now use tools like Hex Threads to produce in minutes analysis that used to take a senior data scientist one to two weeks, and someone with good judgment can move extremely fast toward the right decision with AI's help. He noted Whatnot currently runs just over 20 PMs total, a small team relative to the company's scale of merchandise volume, and those PMs aren't fixed to specific teams — they're reassigned on a six-month planning cadence based on whatever problems matter most at the time. On hiring signals he's increasingly wary of: candidates who spend a lot of interview time talking about "driving alignment" and "stakeholder management," since that flavor of PM's real specialty tends to be office politics rather than technical or customer-facing skill. He spoke at length about a trend he strongly endorses, pushing PMs back into individual-contributor work: historically, a successful PM got promoted into a director role, pulled off the front line into pure coaching, which produced a repeated cycle of work getting done, reviewed, and sent back; at Whatnot now, including himself, most senior people still spend 50% to over 90% of their time doing hands-on work, because senior judgment honed over years of experience makes direct action far faster than three layers of alignment and discussion, and it keeps leadership grounded in ground truth rather than what gets reported up. On failure, he says he's made more wrong calls in his career than right ones, and the most common pattern is trusting averages over individuals: a feature with only 3% overall usage looks safe to cut, but without going a layer deeper you might find that for that 3%, the feature is their entire core use case, and cutting it is devastating for that small group — especially in e-commerce, where an unreliable or removed feature directly hits someone else's business.
items.why: 此条与今日技术主线互为表里：Whatnot 将“核实决策是否正确”的责任从流程移至经验丰富者手中，与 Heiner 和 Davis 所谈评测、协议层核实同源，仅应用场景不同。详见今日可行动第三条及本报社评。
items.why_en: The flip side of today's technical thread from a completely different domain: Whatnot moved "who verifies whether a decision is right" out of process and back onto experienced people, the same underlying idea as Heiner's and Davis's eval- and protocol-layer checkability, applied to a different problem. See the third action item and this issue's synthesis.

items.title: Karpathy 让 Opus 5 把《魔戒》开头渲成 three.js 场景，顺带暴露了模型审不了自己活的短板
items.title_en: Karpathy had Opus 5 render The Lord of the Rings' opening as three.js, and it exposed a real gap: models can't audit their own work
items.author: Hacker News · Andrej Karpathy
items.summary: Andrej Karpathy 今日在 X 上发布新实验，称业内正告别“画一只骑自行车的鹈鹕”这类简单 SVG 测试，他尝试寻找更具泛化性的替代：将《魔戒》第一章交给 Opus 5，提供 100 万 token 预算（约 10 美元），要求其编写一个 three.js 渲染。Opus 运行近两小时，产出 5500 行代码，程序化布置场景、编写动画，效果粗糙但可运行。Karpathy 认为有趣之处在于：没人会手动编写如此定制化的内容，但模型不乏耐心，于是“没人去做”变成“几乎免费，何乐不为”。他进而设想，未来可构建超定制化世界，让人以旁观 NPC 或角色身份进入《魔戒》故事，类似“按需生成的 GTA”。他提到真实短板：游戏与虚拟世界暴露模型弱点，模型无法像人一样直接高效感知视频或在其中互动，Opus 5 只能笨拙地隔段时间截图核对，过程缓慢易错，产生诸多粗糙之处。评论区分歧明显：一部分人讨论视频或游戏生成现状，认为“一句话生成游戏”看似炫目却不好玩，因“好玩”难以优化为训练目标；另一部分人探讨鹈鹕测试的意义，有人建议换以“电影长镜头动画，端到端跑通”等更难题。
items.summary_en: Andrej Karpathy posted a new experiment on X today, saying the industry is starting to leave behind simple SVG tests like "draw a pelican on a bicycle," and he wanted to try something that generalizes further: he gave Opus 5 the first paragraph of The Lord of the Rings, a 1M token budget (about $10), and asked for a three.js render. Opus worked for roughly two hours and produced 5,500 lines of code that procedurally placed and animated the scene, janky but genuinely functional. What he finds interesting about this kind of experiment is that no one in their right mind would ever spend the time hand-writing something this custom, but the model has all the patience in the world, so "no one would ever do this" becomes "sure, why not, it's basically free." He then speculated about building hyper-custom worlds you could drop a person into as a spectator NPC or one of the characters within a story like The Lord of the Rings, something like an on-demand GTA. He closed with a real limitation: the world/game domain exposes a genuine weakness in models, they can't efficiently perceive video or play within these worlds the way a person can, so Opus 5 had to slowly take screenshots at intervals to check its own work, a slow process that produced plenty of mistakes and rough edges. The replies split into two directions: some purely debate the current state of video/game generation, arguing one-shot generated games look flashy but aren't remotely fun, since "fun" itself is nearly impossible to turn into an optimizable training target; others debate whether the pelican test itself still means anything, with some arguing it should be replaced by a harder bar, like rendering a long cinematic scene end-to-end and only counting it as passing if the whole thing actually works.
items.why: 详见今日上手。亦为本报社评要旨：与 Heiner 所谈裁判问题，实为一体两面。
items.why_en: See tonight's hands-on pick. Also a key piece of this issue's synthesis, the flip side of Heiner's grader problem.

items.title: 开放权重之争：微软牵头 235 家公司联署，Anthropic 单独发声反对
items.title_en: The open-weights fight: Microsoft leads 235 companies in a joint letter, Anthropic breaks off with its own response
items.author: 文摘 · Simon Willison
items.summary: Simon Willison 整理了近几周关于 AI 发展路径的公开信。第一封由微软牵头，于 7 月 24 日发布，题为《开放权重与美国 AI 领导地位》，共有 235 家 AI 公司联署，包括英伟达（黄仁勋转发了他人生中第一条推特）、亚马逊、Y Combinator、Linux 基金会，OpenAI 后来也补签。这封信意在说服美国政府不要以“安全”为由限制开放权重模型。信中提出，完全依赖闭源模型并不安全：闭源模型同样可能被攻破或滥用，而且外部难以及时发现；先进能力集中在少数闭源模型上，这会造成单点故障，削弱竞争，让关键技术掌握在少数供应商手中。相比之下，开放权重模型能让更多研究者和开发者检查其行为、发现漏洞、开发防护措施并持续改进。信里一个意外的举动是明确支持“蒸馏”——即用一个模型的输出去训练或改进另一个模型，信中将其视为业界长期存在的常规做法，能促进创新。联署名单中 Anthropic 缺席，这一点引人注目。三天后，Anthropic 发布了《我们对开放权重模型的立场》，CEO Dario Amodei 重申了担忧：威权国家可能利用开放权重模型制造出超越美国的模型，这些模型也可能被滥用于网络攻击或生物武器开发。他呼吁打击“工业规模蒸馏”，但同时也承认自己并不反对开放权重本身。
items.summary_en: Simon Willison compiled the past few weeks of open letters on AI development policy today. The first, led by Microsoft, published July 24th and titled "Open Weights and American AI Leadership," was signed by 235 AI-adjacent companies including NVIDIA (whose CEO Jensen Huang posted his first-ever tweet retweeting the letter), Amazon, Y Combinator, and the Linux Foundation, with OpenAI signing on later. The letter is clearly aimed at heading off any instinct from the current US government to ban or restrict open-weight models on "safety" grounds, arguing that relying solely on closed models isn't inherently safe either — closed models can be breached and misused just as easily, failures are harder for outsiders to detect, and concentrating advanced capability in a handful of closed models creates a small number of single points of failure that weaken competition and hand critical technology to a few providers, whereas open weights let a broad community of researchers examine model behavior, find vulnerabilities, and build safeguards. The letter's one surprising position is explicit support for distillation, training one model on another's outputs, framed as a long-standing, innovation-driving technique rather than something to restrict. Notably absent from the signatures is Anthropic, which published its own "Our position on open-weights models" three days later; CEO Dario Amodei reiterated his concerns that authoritarian governments could use open weights to build models more powerful than America's, that models could be misused for cyberattacks or bioweapons, and called for cracking down on "industrial-scale distillation operations," while also stating Anthropic itself isn't opposed to open weights in principle.
items.why: 这条信息与台账 07-26 的“硬件可移植性审计”相关：谁能获得哪些模型，政策是否限制开放权重，直接影响该线“若 provider 失效，能否切换到开放权重”的前提。值得留意，但今晚无需采取行动。
items.why_en: Relevant to the ledger's 07-26 harness-portability-audit thread: who can access which models, and whether policy ends up restricting open weights, directly affects whether that line's precondition ("can you fail over to an open-weight route when a provider goes down") actually holds. Worth tracking, no action needed tonight.
